derivation: plural of an apparently primary word (properly, meaning very many);
def: ten thousand; by extension, innumerably many

occurrences.text: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, which owed him ten thousand talents.
For though ye have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel.
Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
